questions.question:
Which word best replaces the underlined word in the sentence?

The chef used __a wonderful__ blend of spices to flavour the dish.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4: an exotic**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word "**exotic**" refers to something unusual, striking, or from a distant place, which is fitting when describing a "wonderful blend of spices" that may be unique or foreign in nature.

 
 
• **Example:** The chef used an exotic blend of spices from India to flavour the dish.
 
 
 
• **"Exotic"** is the best replacement because it conveys the idea of something that is appealingly different, which fits well with the context of spices used in cooking to add flavor.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4: an exotic**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *The chef used *an exotic* blend of spices to flavour the dish.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "a bland"** (साधारण, फीका): Refers to something dull or lacking flavor, which is the opposite of a "wonderful blend of spices" that should add distinct flavor.

 
 
• **Example:** The soup was bland and lacked the spices that could make it delicious.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: "an essential"** (आवश्यक): Refers to something necessary, which doesn't fit with the idea of spices adding special flavor to a dish.
 
 
• **Example:** Water is an essential ingredient in many dishes.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: "a supernatural"** (अलौकिक): Refers to something beyond the natural world, which is unrelated to the description of a spice blend used in cooking.
 
 
• **Example:** The movie was full of supernatural events, including magic and mythical creatures.

My friend has gone to Kerala on vacation, but I have no special plans. I will stay home and ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**goof off**'.

__
 
• The phrase "**goof off**" means to relax or waste time in a casual, unproductive way, which fits the context of staying home without any specific plans.
 
• Option 1, "**slip up**," means to make a mistake, which does not fit the context of staying home without plans.
 
• Option 3, "**pitch in**," means to help or contribute, which is unrelated to the context of staying home casually.
 
• Option 4, "**iron out**," means to resolve or clarify something, which doesn't fit the idea of simply staying at home with no special plans.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *"My friend has gone to Kerala on vacation, but I have no special plans. I will stay home and **goof off**__."*

• **Option 4: "iron out"** is incorrect because it refers to resolving or clarifying something, which does not match the casual tone of the sentence.

questions.question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains a grammatical error.

The Chairman instructed the managers that he shall been holding a meeting in Alberto Hall tomorrow evening.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1: shall been holding a meeting**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "**shall been holding**" is grammatically incorrect because "been" should be replaced with "be." The correct phrase is "shall be holding," which uses the correct auxiliary verb structure for future continuous tense.

 
 
• **Example:** He shall be holding a meeting tomorrow evening.
 
 
 
• **"Shall be holding"** is the proper future continuous form, where "shall" indicates future tense, and "holding" is the present participle of the verb "hold."

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1: shall been holding a meeting**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *The Chairman instructed the managers that he shall be holding__ a meeting in Alberto Hall tomorrow evening.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: "managers that he"** (no error): This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **Option 3: "in Alberto Hall tomorrow evening"** (no error): This part of the sentence is also grammatically correct and does not need any changes.
 
• **Option 4: "The Chairman instructed the"** (no error): This part is correct and is a proper subject-verb construction.

• **Example:** The play turned into a farce when the lead actor forgot all his lines.
 
 
 
• **"Tragedy"** refers to a serious event or situation that involves suffering, distress, or a disastrous outcome, often the opposite of farce. (दुःखद घटना)
 
 
• **Example:** The tragic accident left the entire community in mourning.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the opposite of **'farce'** is **'tragedy'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Tragedy**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Mockery** (मज़ाक): Teasing or making fun of someone or something in a contemptuous way.

 
 
• **Example:** His attempt to imitate the teacher turned into a mockery.
 
 
 
• **Charity** (दान): The act of giving help, typically in the form of money, to those in need.
 
 
• **Example:** The organization raises funds for charity to support underprivileged children.
 
 
 
• **Chaos** (अराजकता): Complete disorder and confusion.
 
 
• **Example:** The sudden power outage caused chaos in the shopping mall.

__
 
• The idiom **"Burn the midnight oil"** means to work late into the night, often to complete a task or meet a deadline. (रात में देर तक काम करना)

 
 
• **Example:** She had to burn the midnight oil to finish the project before the deadline.
 
 
 
• **Literal meaning:** If taken literally, it means burning oil in a lamp at midnight, but the figurative meaning is widely used to denote working late hours. (मध्यरात्रि में तेल जलाना)
 
 
• **Example:** During ancient times, scholars used to burn the midnight oil to study by lamplight.

• **Example:** In the past, people burned oil lamps at midnight due to lack of electricity.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: To waste time** (समय बर्बाद करना): This does not align with the actual meaning of the idiom, which refers to productive work rather than wasting time.
 
 
• **Example:** Wasting time is the opposite of burning the midnight oil.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: To extinguish a flame** (ज्वाला को बुझाना): This refers to putting out a fire or flame, which is unrelated to the idiom's meaning.
 
 
• **Example:** The firefighter extinguished the flame quickly.
